brief: Raymond James' weekly wrap frames the S&P 500's recent slide (fifth weekly decline in six weeks, steepest weekly loss since April 2025, 8% off highs) as a correction, not a reversal: this year's worst drawdown (~9%) stays below the ~13% historical average, forward P/E has fallen to its cheapest since 2023, 3Q EPS grew 31% YoY, and the 14-day RSI is approaching oversold near 30-37. It argues the pullback, concentrated in AI-exposed Technology (down 33%, 73% in bear-market territory) and Communication Services (down 28%), sets up buying opportunities since AI buildout and adoption should continue. On rates, the 10-year yield's climb above 5% is driven entirely by rising real yields as markets price over three Fed hikes by June 2027, even as breakevens fall to September 2024 lows; Treasuries have resumed their equity-hedge role. RJ expects one December hike then an extended pause, and calls the dollar's rally potentially stretched. Growth stays resilient (GDP above 2% a quarter, jobless claims near 57-year lows, retail control-group sales up for a third month) despite weak housing (pending sales at a record low, permits at a 2020 low). Hyperscaler AI capex is on pace for $790bn even as new export controls tighten China's access to US computing.
